name: end of life decisions overview
title: End of life: a patient who cannot decide gets a substitute decision maker in a fixed order; palliative care is reached by four routes and aims at comfort; a patient who asks for medical assistance in dying must meet every eligibility criterion, and the stream (natural death foreseeable or not) sets the safeguards; a last IN PRACTICE row gives palliative pearls under palliative care, and how MAiD is delivered plus conscientious objection across both streams

root.title: End of life: who decides, and what can be offered?
lines: capacity (Health Care Consent Act s. 4) = able to UNDERSTAND the information + APPRECIATE the foreseeable consequences of deciding or not · specific to each decision · can fluctuate
code status (which resuscitation, if any) needs informed consent from the patient or SDM · it is NOT the same as goals of care
goals of care: who the patient is, how their values shape their goals, how these fit the clinical picture · prepares for consent decisions
family-centred: dignity and respect for patient, family, significant others throughout

groups.title: Patient asks for medical assistance in dying (MAiD)
lines: legal in Canada June 2016 · 2 streams since March 2021

pres.title: Eligible? ALL of these
lines: • eligible for publicly funded health care
• grievous and irremediable: serious illness, advanced irreversible decline, unbearable suffering not relievable in ways they accept
• informed consent: diagnosis, treatments, ways to relieve suffering including palliative care

head: h
Substitute decision maker (SDM)
gives or refuses consent for the patient
hierarchy: Health Care Consent Act s. 20
do: Ask the SDM, in this ORDER
5 · child (16+), custodial parent or Children's Aid Society
WISHES that guide the SDM, NOT advance consent
~speculation about a future illness, but prepares both

head: h
Palliative care
quality of life: physical, psychosocial, spiritual · patient AND family
team · practical needs · bereavement
when: • treatment futile or would cause suffering
check: • Palliative Performance Scale: disease burden, progress to end of life
• Edmonton Symptom Assessment System: symptoms to manage
do: • stroke, disability unacceptable to them: no tube feeds or IV fluids
• turning and symptom drugs do NOT hasten death
how: • families may be angry when the patient does better
• TEMPORARY improvement, hours to days: reassure
• NOT starving: organs shut down, no hunger or thirst
• patients often die as they lived

head: h
Stream 1
natural death reasonably FORESEEABLE
when: signed before an independent witness (another person may sign if the patient cannot)
do: Consent AGAIN at the time of MAiD
unless a WAIVER of final consent was signed (at risk of losing capacity)

head: h
Stream 2
natural death NOT reasonably foreseeable
check: ONE has expertise in the condition and has discussed all treatment options
do: consent AGAIN at the time of MAiD

rows: • IV: benzodiazepine → high-dose propofol → neuromuscular blocker
• oral lethal drug: an option, rarely used
• no physician has to provide MAiD
• respect dignity · do NOT impede access
• tell the patient directly: a personal, not clinical, reason
